info.name: MediFlow API
info.description:
MediFlow Patient Management System - API collection.

## Setup
1. Start infra: `docker compose up -d` (PostgreSQL + Kafka)
2. Start services with the `seed` profile to load demo users/patients/doctors:
   `mvn -pl backend/auth-service spring-boot:run` (and the other services; the `seed` profile is activated via `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev,seed` or your local convention).
3. Import `MediFlow.postman_environment.json`, select the `MediFlow Local` environment.
4. Run the `01 Auth -> Login (...)` requests once - they auto-store tokens in `adminToken`, `doctorToken`, `patientToken`, `nurseToken`, `billingToken`, `supportToken`.

## Demo users (seed profile)
| Role | Username | Password | Token variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADMIN | `admin` | `Admin@123` | `{{adminToken}}` |
| DOCTOR | `doctor` | `Doctor@123` | `{{doctorToken}}` |
| PATIENT | `patient` | `Patient@123` | `{{patientToken}}` |
| NURSE | `nurse` | `Nurse@123` | `{{nurseToken}}` |
| BILLING_STAFF | `billing` | `Billing@123` | `{{billingToken}}` |
| SUPPORT | `support` | `Support@123` | `{{supportToken}}` |

## Authorization matrix
The backend is authoritative; the same matrix is documented in `docs/security.md`:
- Patient profile: create ADMIN/PATIENT/DOCTOR, update ADMIN/DOCTOR, delete ADMIN, read authenticated (PATIENT scoped to own).
- Doctor profile: create/update ADMIN/DOCTOR (DOCTOR own only), read/search authenticated.
- Appointments: all authenticated; PATIENT/DOCTOR scoped to their own identity, ADMIN/NURSE/BILLING_STAFF/SUPPORT broad.
- Medical records: read ADMIN/DOCTOR(own)/PATIENT(own); NURSE/BILLING_STAFF/SUPPORT denied. Create/update ADMIN/DOCTOR(own); only ADMIN may change `patientId`.
- Billing: writes ADMIN/BILLING_STAFF; reads ADMIN/BILLING_STAFF/DOCTOR/NURSE/SUPPORT and PATIENT (own only).
- Analytics: ADMIN/DOCTOR only.
- Missing/invalid token -> 401; authenticated but not permitted or not the owner -> 403.

## Notes
- All URLs route through the API gateway (`{{gatewayUrl}}`, port 8080).
- Auth is JWT bearer; every protected request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{...Token}}`.
- Login/register/refresh scripts auto-capture `accessToken` + `refreshToken`.
- Folder `09 Authorization (RBAC)` contains negative checks (expected 401/403). Run it after the seed logins; it needs the seeded `{{patientId}}`, `{{doctorId}}`, `{{invoiceId}}` and `{{medicalRecordId}}`.

request.description: The access token presented to /logout is revoked in the shared Redis registry, so it is rejected immediately here (auth-service) and by every other service that validates the token. This must return 401.

item.name: 09 Authorization (RBAC)
item.description: Negative and positive authorization checks for the documented role matrix. Run after the seed logins. Expected failures are assertions, not errors: 401 = no/invalid token, 403 = authenticated but role/ownership not permitted.

item.name: Reassign medical record patient as DOCTOR -> 403
10 Account Lifecycle (ADMIN)
item.description: Administrative identity lifecycle. Every change revokes all sessions of the target account.

request.description: All sessions of the target are revoked; its previously issued access tokens are rejected everywhere.
Roles are embedded in access tokens, so every session of the target is revoked and a new login is required.

item.name: 11 Password Security (destructive)
item.description: Destructive password flows. They revoke every session of the affected account - run them last and update the login bodies afterwards.

request.description: Responds identically for unknown addresses. Returns data.token only when AUTH_PASSWORD_RESET_EXPOSE_TOKEN=true (local/dev).
Single-use token; revokes all sessions. Needs AUTH_PASSWORD_RESET_EXPOSE_TOKEN=true to run end to end locally.
Requires the current password, then revokes every session of the caller (including the token used here).
